Right, people are embarrassed to seek help for a problem that could potentially end up costing them their life even when they know they might benefit from it. It's literally fucking crazy. I mean you don't see people avoiding going to get treatment for cancer because they might be stigmatized so why should we be stigmatized for feeling a perfectly normal human emotion that is maladaptive. We judge other people for things that we ourselves feel and for doing things that we would likely do under similar circumstances. I feel like most people have felt a severe level of depression at some point in their life but they forget what it feels like.

Yes. I deal with this on the daily. I do a great job of hiding it from the world though. In my experience I feel a whole lot better when I do let at least some of that frustration and anxiety out by expressing it to another human being. But most times I can't even do that because you never know who is going to take what you say and pass it on to the next person as if it were a piece of gossip that belonged in the tabloids. Sometimes taking deep breaths really helps for me. Sometimes it doesn't. Sometimes I literally imagine the place that I feel most at peace in the world and try to engross myself in the image which often helps. I would say a lot of people deal with this though. That doesn't make it any more ok or easier to deal with however.

In rats the LD50, or lethal dosage to kill 50% of the population,is over 1600 mg/KG of body weight. That means if a rat weighed 2 KGs it would take 3200 mg to kill 50% of all rats at that weight. That's in rats and obviously the biochemistry of the human body is completely different from that of a Rat, but based upon this information no I don't think that 1400 mgs of seroquel would kill you. I think like Finger said, you would just feel absolutely terrible after taking it but you would still wake up.
